reasons: No test is visible for the page or for how it handles unexpected data from the server.
The fallback backend address is a local development address, so a missing setting will fail quietly in real use.
The file uses loose types, so data shape errors appear only at run time.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and backend address
sections.what: Brings in the tools for the page, including the icons, date formatting, and the request library. It also sets the backend address, which can come from a setting or fall back to a local address.
sections.why: The backend address must be set correctly so the page can reach the shared records.
sections.watch_out: The local fallback address will not work on a real site unless the setting is provided.

sections.name: DoctorPortalPage (part 1)
sections.title: Fetching the shared records
sections.what: Reads the token from the web address, asks the backend for the shared records, and stores the result. It also records any error message and turns off the loading state when finished.
sections.why: The page needs the records before it can show anything, and it must handle the case where the link is no longer valid.
sections.watch_out: The error text from the server is shown to the visitor, so the server must not send sensitive details in error messages.

sections.name: DoctorPortalPage: if
sections.title: Loading and access denied screens
sections.what: Shows a spinner with 'Loading Patient Records' while the request runs. If the request failed or returned nothing, shows an 'Access Restricted' notice with a privacy note.
sections.why: Gives the doctor a clear message in both cases instead of a blank page.
sections.watch_out: The notice mentions privacy rules, which is fixed text and not a legal check.

sections.name: DoctorPortalPage (part 3)
sections.title: Header and patient banner
sections.what: Shows the top bar with the Maate name, a Clinician Portal label, and a read-only note. The main area then shows the patient's name, gender, date of birth, blood group, when access expires, and which resources were shared.
sections.why: Lets the doctor confirm who the patient is and how long they can see the records.
sections.watch_out: The page reads the expiry date and shared resources directly from the server data, so a missing expiry value will cause a display error.

sections.name: DoctorPortalPage (part 4)
sections.title: Document list with AI summaries and lab tables
sections.what: Lists each shared document with its title, type, and report date, and a link to open the original file. When present, it also shows the AI summary with recommendations and a table of lab test results with status colors.
sections.why: Gives the doctor the documents and the key findings in one place.
sections.watch_out: The AI summary is a machine-written summary and should be checked against the original document before a doctor relies on it.

sections.name: DoctorPortalPage (part 5)
sections.title: Active medicines list
sections.what: Shows each shared medicine with its name, how often it is taken, its dose, meal timing, and daily schedule. If nothing is shared it shows a 'No active medication' message.
sections.why: Lets the doctor check what the patient is currently taking.
sections.watch_out: The page shows whatever the patient shared, so the list may not be complete.

sections.name: DoctorPortalPage (part 6)
sections.title: Recent vital signs list
sections.what: Shows up to eight of the most recent vital sign readings, each with its type, time, value, and status. If there are none, it says no vital signs were recorded.
sections.why: Gives a quick view of recent measurements such as blood pressure or heart rate.
sections.watch_out: Only the first eight readings are shown, so older readings are hidden and the list order depends on the server.

sections.name: DoctorPortalPage (part 7)
sections.title: Vital signs list on doctor page
sections.what: Shows the latest vital sign readings in a list on the shared doctor view. If there are none, it shows a short 'No vital signs recorded' message. Each row shows the reading type, when it was measured, the value with any second value and unit, and a status word. It shows at most eight readings.
sections.why: Likely reason: the doctor sees a quick summary of recent readings without opening the full record. Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Each row reads measuredAt and passes it to a date parser, so a reading with a missing or badly formatted date may break the page; the code does not check for this, and it assumes the list is already sorted newest first, which this section does not do.

summary: A public, read-only page where a doctor can view a patient's shared records using a secret link token.
purpose: Lets a clinician see the documents, medicines, and vitals a patient chose to share, for the time the link is valid.
why: The patient controls access with an expiring, revocable link, so the doctor does not need an account to view the records.
how: It reads the token from the web address and asks the backend for the shared data. While waiting it shows a loading message. If the link is invalid or expired it shows an 'Access Restricted' message. Otherwise it shows the patient's details, documents with any AI summary and lab tables, active medicines, and up to eight recent vitals.
inputs: The token in the web address, and the backend address from the environment setting, which falls back to a local development address.
outputs: A read-only clinical view of the shared patient information. Nothing can be edited.
risks: Anyone holding the link can see the patient's medical data, so the link must be kept private. The fallback backend address points to a local machine, which would fail in a real deployment if the setting is missing. The page also trusts the shape of the data from the server and uses loose types, so unexpected data may break the page.
debug: If the page says the link is invalid when it should work, check the backend route for the share view and the token's expiry. If the page never loads, check the NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL setting. If a section is missing, check that the server returns the matching field name.
